lines.text: This salamander regrows its legs, its heart, even parts of its brain.

lines.text: Meet the axolotl, the salamander that never grows up.

parts.tts: Meet the axolotl, the salamander that never grows up.
parts.heard: Meet the axolotl, the salamander that never grows up.

lines.text: It keeps its larval body for life, frilly gills and all.

parts.tts: It keeps its larval body for life, frilly gills and all.
parts.heard: It keeps its larval body for life, frilly gills and all.

lines.text: Lose a leg? A new one grows back within months.

parts.tts: Lose a leg? A new one grows back within months.
parts.heard: Lose a leg? A new one grows back within months.

lines.text: But that's just the start. Its tail, its spinal cord, even parts of its heart grow back, without scars.

parts.tts: But that's just the start. Its tail, its spinal cord, even parts of its heart grow back, without scars.
parts.heard: But that's just the start. Its tail, its spinal cord, even parts of its heart grow back without scars.

lines.text: But here's the wild part. It can rebuild parts of its brain.

parts.tts: But here's the wild part. It can rebuild parts of its brain.
parts.heard: But here's the wild part. It can rebuild parts of its brain.

lines.text: Scientists study it, hoping humans could one day heal like this.

parts.tts: Scientists study it, hoping humans could one day heal like this.
parts.heard: Scientists study it, hoping humans could one day heal like this.

lines.text: But in the wild, the axolotl is critically endangered.

parts.tts: But in the wild, the axolotl is critically endangered.
parts.heard: But in the wild, the axolotl is critically endangered.

lines.text: It's down to a few canals near Mexico City, with maybe 50 to 1,000 adults left.
